The most requested feature is here: **notifications** on AWTRIX NG. 🔔 Update from the Marketplace (HACS on Home Assistant 2026.10 or older), restart Home Assistant, and you're set: your apps keep working as they are.

## 🔔 Notifications (AWTRIX NG)

A notification interrupts whatever the clock is showing, the moment something happens in your home, and goes away when it is over. No automation to write, nothing added to your history database.

- 🚪 **The doorbell rings:** a bell icon and "Someone at the door" for 30 seconds, with a melody.
- 🌧️ **It starts raining:** "It's raining", shown once, not every time the sensor hesitates.
- ⛈️ **A storm is coming:** "Storm at 12 km", the distance read from a sensor when the alert starts.
- 🪟 **A window was left open:** on screen until it is closed.

### 📍 Where to find it

Open **Awtrix Studio** in the sidebar and pick your AWTRIX NG clock. Then **scroll to the bottom of the page**: the **Notifications** section sits **below the Indicators**, after all your apps. Click **Add notification** there.

The section only shows up for a clock running AWTRIX NG (Ulanzi TC001 or TC002). On an AWTRIX 3 clock you won't see it.

### 🛠️ Set one up in a minute

1. **What triggers it.** Pick the entity (your doorbell, rain sensor, window contact…) and the state that shows the notification: `on`, `open`, `home`… The states of the entity are offered in a list, and **Other…** lets you type one. This entity only triggers the notification: it is not shown unless you add it below.
2. **What it shows.** One or two lines, each a text, the value of an entity (with its unit, decimals and color by value), or both. On a TC002, choose **One line**, **Two lines** or **Title and value**, with a font and a position for each line. Add an icon from the LaMetric gallery, as for an app.
3. **How it is shown.** A duration, scroll repeats, a sound (the name of a melody stored on the clock, `alarm` for `MELODIES/alarm.txt`), **Stay until dismissed**, and **Queue behind other notifications** or replace the one on screen.
4. **When it goes away.** **Take it off when the state ends** dismisses it as soon as the door is answered or the window closed. A **Delay before it can show again** keeps a sensor that goes on and off from showing it again too soon (60 minutes for a rain sensor, say).

The preview shows the exact message sent to the clock, and **Send to the clock to test** tries it right away (it is taken off after 15 seconds). Each notification gets its own switch in Home Assistant, and is included in export and import. Template mode is there too, for the firmware's own JSON.

### ✅ It behaves

- **Only real changes.** Nothing is sent when Home Assistant starts, or when the entity comes back from being unavailable: only when it really enters the state.
- **It never touches other notifications.** Each one has its own name and is dismissed by that name, so a notification sent by another automation stays on screen.
- **Nothing is lost in silence.** A notification too large for the clock is not sent, and one the clock refuses is reported: either way the panel says why, next to the notification.

## ✨ Also new

- ⚡ **Changes applied without reloading the clock.** Adding, editing or removing an app, an indicator or a notification now only updates that item: the others are not sent again, and the panel keeps its place.
- 🔗 **The clock's address on the overview,** as a link to its own web page.

## 🐛 Fixed

- 🧭 **An ignored discovery broke the list of clocks.** Ignoring an AWTRIX NG clock that Home Assistant had found left the panel unable to list the clocks.
- 🔁 **Reconfiguring a clock onto an ignored discovery.** The ignored entry is now removed, so two entries never share a prefix.
- 🖥️ **The screen mirror after switching clocks.** The previous clock's screen no longer keeps drawing over the new one.

## ⬆️ Updating

Nothing to do: your apps, icons and settings are kept. Notifications need AWTRIX NG; on an AWTRIX 3 clock, everything else in this release applies as usual.
